extracted.intended_audience: SNSF decision-makers, research policy analysts, host-institution administrators, and prospective Ambizione applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation guidance and criteria for assessing the Ambizione career funding scheme (concept, implementation, reach, impacts on grantees and hosts, and monitoring). Intended to inform policymaking, scheme design changes, and monitoring practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept of the Ambizione funding scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the goals, the design (extent of the grant, funding criteria and requirements, additional support, etc.) and the target groups of Ambizione suitable? Is Ambizione harmonised with other (similar) funding instruments of the SNSF?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate adequacy and coherence of the funding concept, including flexibility of regulations (allowing case-by-case assessments) and alignment/harmonisation with other SNSF instruments. Consider whether design features (budget size, duration, scope) match target groups' needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation by the SNSF
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the support that the SNSF offers Ambizione grantees sufficient? How well does the SNSF implement the scheme?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess grantees' appreciation of SNSF support; check administrative processes, clarity of information, and whether SNSF supervision ensures equal treatment and uniform application of rules. Look for evidence from surveys/interviews about the quality of SNSF support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation by host institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Are grantees supported adequately by the host institutions? How are the collaboration between hosts and grantees and the integration of the grantees into the host institutions evaluated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine hosts' provision of support (personnel, financial, equipment), integration of grantees into research/teaching, mismatches of expectations, and any difficulties. Consider host-side variability and proposals for oversight (e.g., independent office).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach of the Ambizione funding scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the target groups defined in the Ambizione funding scheme concept reached? Does Ambizione satisfy the needs and requirements of the target groups?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether main targets (e.g., returnees, incoming foreign talent) are reached and whether the scheme meets their specific needs. Use composition statistics (e.g., nationality, mobility) and survey feedback on fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on grantees — scientific independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Have Ambizione grantees been able to carry out their research projects (more) independently? Were their research projects successfully completed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use self-assessed and host-assessed measures of independence (Likert items), evidence of project completion, and qualitative accounts of what independence means in different disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on grantees — scientific profile and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the Ambizione grant enhanced the scientific profile of the grantees (e.g. through publications, awards, conference participation, or further research endeavours)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess changes in publication quantity and quality, awards, conference activity, networking, visibility ('works as a label'), and subsequent research projects. Use survey items like increased number/quality of publications and enhanced scientific profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on grantees — career progression
rubrics_metrics.description: Have Ambizione grantees successfully carried on with their scientific careers? Has there been a career step (e.g. tenure track position, professorship, group leader position, etc.), and to what extent has Ambizione contributed to this career step?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track career outcomes (positions, tenure-track, professorships, group leader roles), subsequent funding received, location of employment (Switzerland/abroad), and self-reported contribution of Ambizione to these steps. Use comparison groups to estimate relative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on hosts (benefits and disadvantages)
rubrics_metrics.description: In what ways do the host institutions benefit from hiring Ambizione grantees (e.g. in terms of scientific exchange or a boost to the scientific performance of the institution)? Did hosts encounter difficulties integrating Ambizione grantees?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate benefits (expanded scientific profile, additional research activity, teaching resources, financial gain, supervision) and any disadvantages (integration difficulties, false expectations). Use host survey items on benefits and collaboration quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching goals attainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Has Ambizione generated knowledge transfer into Switzerland? Has Ambizione helped researchers from Switzerland doing research abroad return to the Swiss scientific community? Is Ambizione an attractive funding scheme for young talents from abroad? Has Ambizione had specific effects in terms of gender?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contribution to knowledge transfer, reintegration of returnees, attractiveness to incoming researchers, capability to fund low-mobility researchers, and gender-related effects (e.g., female participation rates versus the 35% target). Use quantitative indicators and qualitative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a doctorate (PhD) obtained generally up to five years prior to submission; MD applicants must have completed at least three years of post-graduate clinical/practical work and may apply up to nine years after medical licence; applicants must furnish proof of high-level publications; applicants must have completed postdoctoral research activities lasting at least 12 months at a university other than the one that conferred the doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check applicants' CVs and documentation against these temporal and achievement thresholds. Consider allowable exceptions and discipline-specific interpretations where regulation flexibility applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host letter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione grant applications must include a letter from the host institution confirming it will provide the applicant adequate support in covering research expenses and including a statement on the independence and scientific autonomy of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit host confirmation of support and applicant independence; use host letter as evidence in eligibility and assessment phases. Review letters for clarity and concrete commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding features (budget and duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione grantees are supported with a budget of up to CHF 600,000 for a salary (research associate level) and research funds for a maximum period of three years; research funds may also be used to employ personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify awarded budgets adhere to maxima; evaluate whether budget and duration are appropriate for proposed projects; examine proposals to use funds for personnel and how that affects project feasibility. Consider policy discussions about extending duration to four years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation procedure and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation procedure is organised in two phases: first the National Research Council (NRC) makes an initial selection based on submitted documents; second, applications are peer-reviewed and candidates are invited to an interview to present their project and career plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess transparency and robustness of both phases, the quality of peer review and interview assessment, and whether initial selection criteria are consistently applied. Note that regulations allow case-by-case assessments due to scheme flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-experimental comparative evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of two comparison groups in the surveys: (1) researchers with rejected Ambizione applications (2008–2013) and (2) researchers who received SNSF project funding in the same period, to assess Ambizione's relative impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When measuring effects, use comparison groups to control for selection effects. Evaluate baseline equivalence and account for differences in applicant populations when interpreting impact estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring concept (cohort design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested monitoring design: invite former Ambizione grantees to participate in a survey right after their funding ends and again four years later, to gather short-term and long-term career information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement cohort surveys using a shortened version of the evaluation questionnaire; ensure follow-up rates, maintain contact databases, and schedule waves to capture short- and medium-term outcomes (e.g., career progression, publications, job location).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation — allow funding of scientific personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees requested the possibility to use part of the Ambizione grant to employ scientific personnel (doctoral students or postdocs); this change has been implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess impact of allowing personnel hiring on project output, supervision load, and host support needs; monitor how funds are allocated and whether this addresses grantees' most frequently mentioned improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation — extend funding duration from 3 to 4 years
rubrics_metrics.description: The funding period of three years is considered too short and should be increased to four years; the SNSF supports this idea and implementation has been discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model effects of a longer funding period on project completion rates, career outcomes, and budget implications. Use pilot or retrospective comparisons where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation — ensure equal treatment and uniform host implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: SNSF should continuously supervise equal treatment of Ambizione grantees and the equal implementation of the scheme by host institutions; hosts suggested creating an independent office for these tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider oversight mechanisms, standardized host agreements, guidelines for integration and independence guarantees, and possibly an independent unit to monitor host compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender target and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeted share of female grantees is 35%; female participation has been fairly constant on average but there was a drop in 2013 that should be monitored and the target regularly discussed and possibly revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track sex-disaggregated application and success rates annually, investigate causes of fluctuations, and use targets as policy levers. Include gender-sensitive indicators in monitoring and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey impact indicators (grantee questionnaire items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey items used to measure impact include: improved competence in field; enhanced scientific profile; increased scientific competitiveness; improved (international) networking; easier access to leading scientists; increased number of publications; improved quality of publications; enabled foothold in the Swiss science scene after a stay abroad; ability to carry out the project without the grant; contribution of Ambizione to career steps; subsequent funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Likert scales to quantify perceived impacts; triangulate self-reports with bibliometrics, grant records, and host assessments for more objective measures. Include open-ended follow-ups for qualitative nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host survey metrics and items
rubrics_metrics.description: Host-side questionnaire covers motivations to host (reputation of researcher/Ambizione, knowledge transfer, complementarity), benefits (expanded profile, teaching, extra funds, supervision), assessment of collaboration and integration quality, research project quality, extent to guarantee independence, ongoing employment after funding, and perceived impacts on grantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect host ratings (very good/good/rather bad/very bad) and benefit assessments (very accurate/rather accurate/etc.). Use these to cross-validate grantee responses and identify recurrent host-level issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target group classification and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and codes for applicant types (incoming, returning, limited mobility), with subcategories based on Swiss passport status, PhD location, application origin, and prior SNSF fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standardized classification when analysing reach and outcomes (e.g., Inc_A, Inc_CH, Ret_Pass_A, etc.). Use these categories to stratify impact analyses and monitor whether the scheme serves intended target groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of qualitative methods (expert interviews and case studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert interviews (n=7) and case studies (n=10) with former grantees were used to obtain qualitative insights on the funding scheme and to supplement survey data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate qualitative findings to contextualize quantitative results, identify field-specific issues, and derive further research questions. Ensure case study selection mirrors distribution of discipline, gender, and applicant category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of integration and differences versus other postdocs
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether Ambizione grantees differ from other postdocs in scientific independence, responsibilities, and integration into the host; ask hosts whether the grantee was different and scientifically more independent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use host comparisons and survey items to detect structural differences (e.g., independence, additional resources). Investigate any systemic patterns where Ambizione grantees are treated differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation — use shortened survey instrument for monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: For regular monitoring, use a short version of the online questionnaire developed for the evaluation to follow grantees’ careers over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a concise instrument capturing core outcome indicators (career position, location, publications, further funding, perceived impact) to minimize respondent burden and maximize response rates in cohort follow-ups.
